title: Alkali-promoted Fe-based multimetallic catalysts for CO 2  hydrogenation to C 2+  chemicals: from reaction mechanism to catalyst development
content: Catalytic hydrogenation of CO2 to value-added chemicals is one of the promising pathways for achieving carbon neutrality, addressing energy and climate challenges. Alkali-promoted Fe-based multimetallic catalysts, enabling the direct synthesis of C2+ chemicals in one step, have stimulated growing interest due to their outstanding performance. However, the multimetallic synergistic effect and complex structural evolution pose a significant challenge in understanding the structure–activity relationship and developing new catalysts. In this review, we focus on a deep understanding of the structure–activity relationship through a systematic analysis of recent advances in understanding the reaction mechanism, active phase, and structural evolution of Fe-based catalysts in CO2 hydrogenation. Several key roles of metal promoters in Fe-based catalysts are summarized and discussed, including construction of key active sites, stabilization of the active phase and regulation of the carburization process, and optimization and modulation of the active-phase electronic structure. The design and preparation of multi-metal promoted Fe-based catalysts and construction of multifunctional catalysts with zeolites are also comprehensively discussed. Ultimately, we put forward prospects for future development of high-performance Fe-based catalysts.
